messages.subject: Warning Message: Didn't converge!
parts:
Hi,

I'm getting Warning Message : Didn't Converge! when re-estimate the genetic map and plot the original map against the newly estimated one. 

What does it mean? Is it ok to ignore this warning message.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Warning Message: Didn't converge!
parts:
The estimation of inter-marker distances uses an iterative algorithm, in which the estimates are gradually improved over many small steps. The algorithm is halted when the maximum absolute difference in the recombination fractions is less than "tol" (default 10^-6), in which case we say the estimates "converged"; it is alternatively halted if the number of iterations reaches "maxit" (default 10000), in which case a warning message is printed.

I would generally repeat the call to est.map(), starting at the new map. You might also increase the value of "maxit". Here's an example:

library(qtl)
data(hyper)
newmap <- est.map(hyper, err=0.01)
hyper_newmap <- replacemap(hyper, newmap)
newmap2 <- est.map(hyper_newmap, err=0.01, maxit=100000)

You might also make the "tol" value less stringent (say 10^-4) so that the algorithm meets the convergence criterion in a small number of iterations. But doing this, or ignoring the warning message, will mean that the estimated map will be not as good as it could be. But the difference may not matter.

Missing genotype data really slows down the estimation of the genetic map. I've found it sometimes useful to get an initial estimate the map using filled-in genotypes and then refine that using the actual data, something like this:

library(qtl)
data(hyper)
hyper_filled <- fill.geno(hyper)
initmap <- est.map(hyper_filled)
hyper <- replacemap(hyper, initmap)
newmap <- est.map(hyper, err=0.01)

karl
